summary: SSE reconnect write-window clash causes orphaned HTML tags and missing final metadata during proxy downgrade
description:
Issue summary: Several customers (first reported by QuillPulse) see HTML snippets in streamed responses that are left with unclosed tags (e.g.,
without
) and missing final metadata envelope when client reconnects after an edge proxy downgrades from HTTP/2 to HTTP/1.1. Impact: partial/corrupt UX on customer apps, embedded links/attachments missing, downstream parsers reject final payloads. Environment: prod (us-east) behind a corp transparent proxy that performs protocol downgrade and chunked rewrapping. Occurs intermittently during bursts and on client reconnects. Expected: on reconnect the stream resumes logically without producing orphaned markup or dropping the final metadata envelope. Actual: server appears to accept resumed prefix but a write-window race between proxy and SSE streamer leaves trailing open tags and strips the concluding metadata event. This is reproducible for the customer under a short test harness (steps below).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Initiate a long SSE stream generation using rl hf-32k-v1 in prod us-east from a browser client behind corporate proxy that downgrades h2->h1.
2) During an active stream, simulate a short edge path churn (close the socket) so client reconnects and attempts resume via our session token prefix replay.
3) Observe server accept of resume and client receiving a duplicated prefix; simultaneously the edge-proxy performs chunked rewrap and emits a final FIN that races with the resumed payload.

4) Inspect client event stream: look for partial UTF-8 emoji sequences broken across chunk boundaries, HTML tags that remain unclosed, and missing final metadata event (e.g., closing {"type":"done","meta":...}).
logs: client-observed: partial-utf8="\uD83D\uDE" (truncated emoji), received-events=[data, data, data, heartbeat, data] no done event
investigation: Initial triage by support showed a tight timing window between edge FIN handling and resumed payload flush from SSE streamer.
Hypothesis A: edge-proxy chunk rewrap drops zero-length final delimiter when it sees resumed payload overlapping FIN handling. This results in server-side final-metadata write being lost on the wire.

Hypothesis B: client-side prefix replay combined with downstream chunk-coalescing creates malformed UTF-8 boundaries and leaves an open HTML tag when server-sent incremental fragments are cut mid-tag.

Reproduce in lab by running a proxy shim that intentionally downgrades h2->h1 and injecting a 5-10ms artificial close during resumed window. Lab reproduction consistent with customer symptoms in 9/10 runs.

Captured tcpdump on the server-side shows final JSON metadata write but downstream ack never arrives; edge proxy log shows final chunk was rewritten and FIN raced with resumed content (timestamps within 2ms).
comments: 2026-03-10 15:00 - Aisha Patel (Support): Customer provided two example payloads with unclosed <div> and missing done envelope. Asked for network captures and the client's proxy header. (attachments: partial_stream_1.txt, pcap_quillpulse_0310.pcap)

2026-03-10 16:20 - Marcus Liu (SRE): Confirmed lab reproduction; opened hypothesis ticket with edge team. Noted the SSE streamer flush path writes final-metadata after sending all token fragments; if TCP FIN is processed by the proxy during the write, proxy's chunk rewriter can drop the trailing delimiter.

2026-03-11 09:05 - Elena Rodriguez (Edge Team): Edge patch candidate created to ensure rewrite preserves trailing delimiter when write-window contains simultaneous FIN+payload. PR: github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy@pr/4271

2026-03-11 11:40 - QuillPulse (Customer): Reporting that the issue causes their in-app renderer to hang waiting for closing tag; provided user-facing screenshot. Asked whether there is a temporary workaround server-side.

2026-03-11 13:10 - Marcus Liu (SRE): Recommended temporary mitigation: disable HTTP/2->HTTP/1.1 downgrade at proxy level (if possible) or enable client-side tolerance (buffer incoming stream until done event) as a short-term workaround. We will test edge patch in staging and backport to prod if green.
resolution: Workaround recommended to customer: if their proxy can be configured to avoid h2->h1 downgrade or to preserve zero-length delimiters, that prevents corruption. Edge team created PR to make chunk rewriter preserve trailing delimiter and to add a 5ms jitter in FIN handling to avoid races. Patch deployed to staging 2026-03-11, tests show resolution of orphaned-tags and metadata loss in lab harness (10/10 runs). Next steps: schedule canary deploy to us-east low-traffic zone, monitor token-level metrics and stream 'done' event delivery for 24h, then roll to remaining hosts. Related PRs: github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy@pr/4271, github.com/redwood-inference/sse-streamer@pr/902. Continue to monitor customer until canary completes.
